note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/sign-in.reason: cinatra#2616 the agent_templates identity claim: ONE new first-party module, packages/agents/src/agent-template-identity.ts, becomes reachable from all five locked routes. package_name is globally unique, so it is an instance-wide identity, and the publish/install primitive upserted by that name with no organization predicate — a publish under a name another organization held ADOPTED its row. The guard has to be a predicate ANDed into the writes inside store.ts (that is what makes the claim atomic rather than a checked-then-upserted read), so store.ts must import the rule, and store.ts is on every locked route. The module cannot be avoided: store.ts sits EXACTLY at its own file-size-ratchet ceiling, which may only ever be lowered, so the claim had to be carried by an extraction — the thin-facade + vertical-slice pattern that ratchet prescribes. It was minimised to ONE: the rule and its operations were drafted as two files (a leaf for the predicate, a tier above for the operations) and merged back into one precisely because a second file would have cost a second module on all five routes for no architectural gain. The module imports only ./db and ./schema, never ./store, so it adds no cross-package edge and no barrel; the extraction also moved the origin writers and the packageName derivation OUT of store.ts, so the first-party module the routes gain replaces graph that was already there. Counts measured by CI on the PR merge commit with the companion extension repos cloned pinned.
